bibl.title: The predictive global neuronal workspace: A formal active inference model of visual consciousness

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: The core notion underlying our model is that conscious access is a fundamentally inferential process that can only occur at a level of processing that is sufficiently temporally deep to integrate information from lower levels of the hierarchy and contextualise processing at these lower levels.

span.label: visual consciousness (conscious access)
span.quote: However, this paper is chiefly concerned with what Block (2005) terms “access consciousness” which is defined as the availability of information for verbal report, voluntary action, and executive processing.

span.label: simulation
span.quote: We report simulations demonstrating the model’s ability to reproduce: 1) the electrophysiological and behaviour results observed in previous studies of inattentional blindness; and 2) the previously introduced four-way taxonomy predicted by the GNW, which describes the relationship between consciousness, attention, and sensory signal strength.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Conscious access happens because a temporally deep level of the hierarchy infers and integrates lower-level states over a slow enough timescale to contextualise them and drive extended report behaviour.
span.quote: The core notion underlying our model is that conscious access is a fundamentally inferential process that can only occur at a level of processing that is sufficiently temporally deep to integrate information from lower levels of the hierarchy and contextualise processing at these lower levels.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Late ERPs arise because the ERP is the time derivative of the depolarisation variable, so a rapid change in high-level belief produces a large late deflection.
span.quote: ERPs and local field potentials are modelled as the time derivative (rate of change) of the depolarisation variable because the change in membrane potential over neuronal populations is what generates ERPs.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Rapid belief change increases the magnitude of the depolarisation derivative, which is what makes a late component appear.
span.quote: When confidence in a state changes rapidly, the derivative of the depolarisation variable increases in magnitude.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Expectations act by raising second-level posterior confidence, which magnifies top-down feedback to sensory populations and pushes marginal trials past the ignition threshold.
span.quote: Consistent expectations increase second-level posterior confidence to a sufficiently large degree to shift otherwise unconscious trials over the threshold for “ignition” by magnifying the feedback to the first level

span.label: Scope deliberately restricted to settings where visual consciousness is operationalised by report.
span.quote: To make the PGNW testable, we have deliberately limited the scope of the model to experimental settings where visual consciousness is operationalised via report.

span.label: Report paradigms themselves carry known methodological problems.
span.quote: However, we acknowledge that report paradigms come with methodological difficulties (Tsuchiya et al., 2015).

span.label: Restricting the model to vision perpetuates the visual bias of consciousness science.
span.quote: By the same token, in limiting the scope of the PGNW to the visual modality, we are aware that we are reifying the pervasive bias in consciousness science of primarily studying vision.

span.label: The match to the four-way taxonomy is partly built in, since parameters were tuned to the published behavioural results.
span.quote: This should not be a surprise, as we finetuned the parameter values to capture behaviour reported in the empirical literature.

span.label: The model cannot represent partial awareness, because information cannot skip hierarchical levels in it.
span.quote: This requires information to skip levels of the hierarchy, which is also not possible in the present model.

span.label: Simulated report frequencies are only directional, not quantitative, predictions.
span.quote: Finally, it must be highlighted that the behavioural results of the following simulations should be interpreted as directional hypotheses, as opposed to precise predictions about the percentage of seen vs unseen trials.

span.label: Two predictions of the theory this paper extends are stated to have been falsified.
span.quote: Of greater concern is the fact that, as experimental paradigms have become more sophisticated, two predictions of the original theory have been falsified

span.label: The falsifying result is qualified inline by whether its instrument is a fair proxy.
span.quote: Together these results demonstrate that, contrary to the original formulation of the GNW, information is processed and unconsciously maintained (at least briefly and insofar as multivariate decoding is a defensible proxy for information processing) by the same structures implicated in conscious processing

span.label: The P3 is reported to track task relevance rather than conscious access.
span.quote: This result was recently replicated in a standard masking paradigm (Cohen, et al., 2020) showing unequivocally that the P3 is related to task relevance and is not a necessary signature of conscious access

span.label: A marker was abandoned without any accompanying theoretical revision, which the authors name as a degenerative pattern.
span.quote: In addition, the abandonment of the P3 as a signature of conscious access was not accompanied by any theoretical revisions and makes no additional behavioural or neurobiological predictions. This situates the GNW in a tenuous position, in which revision primarily explains away contrary results – a recognized characteristic of degenerative research programs

span.label: The replacement model offered for the falsified one is stated to be too idealised for neurobiological predictions.
span.quote: However, the modified computational model of subjective report (King & Dehaene, 2014) is too idealised to make neurobiological predictions

span.label: Where phenomenology sits in the model was chosen to avoid an empirically unfalsifiable consequence.
span.quote: i.e., the presence of a particular phenomenology would become empirically unfalsifiable). To avoid this uncomfortable conclusion, while also keeping sensory phenomenology at the correct timescale, we suggest that phenomenology in our model is most plausibly situated at the point during which (and based on the manner in which) lower-level representations update the content of higher-level states

span.label: A parameter that empirical work fits to data was fixed by assumption, and it affects the predicted ERPs.
span.quote: there is an optional parameter (mdp.erp) that encodes the assumed degree of decay or attenuation in posterior beliefs across timesteps (i.e., before each period of gradient descent following each new observation). In empirical work, this parameter needs to be fit to neuronal or behavioural responses. Here we do not include this parameter (i.e., we set it to a value of 1), which entails that posterior beliefs at one timepoint fully carry over as priors for the subsequent timepoint in a trial. This is analogous to predictive coding formulations and is most appropriate for our simulations due to the fact that multiple timepoints in our simulated trials are treated as single observations (i.e., there should be no attenuation or ‘resetting’ of priors within a single stimulus presentation). It is important to note this here, however, as predicted ERPs in simulations can be affected by different values of this parameter

span.label: the P3 - A MARKER WITHDRAWN WITHOUT A REVISION: the claim that it is a specific marker of conscious access is no longer defended, but the abandonment was not accompanied by any theoretical revisions and makes no additional predictions, which the authors call a recognized characteristic of degenerative research programs
span.quote: In addition, the abandonment of the P3 as a signature of conscious access was not accompanied by any theoretical revisions and makes no additional behavioural or neurobiological predictions. This situates the GNW in a tenuous position, in which revision primarily explains away contrary results – a recognized characteristic of degenerative research programs

span.label: the falsifying evidence - CONDITIONAL ON A PROXY: information is said to be unconsciously maintained by the same structures at least briefly and insofar as multivariate decoding is a defensible proxy for information processing, so the result that overturns the theory is bounded by an instrument assumption stated in its own sentence
span.quote: Together these results demonstrate that, contrary to the original formulation of the GNW, information is processed and unconsciously maintained (at least briefly and insofar as multivariate decoding is a defensible proxy for information processing) by the same structures implicated in conscious processing

span.label: phenomenology, in this model - SITED TO KEEP IT FALSIFIABLE: the alternative placement would make the presence of a particular phenomenology empirically unfalsifiable, and the authors situate it at the point where lower-level representations update higher-level states to avoid that
span.quote: i.e., the presence of a particular phenomenology would become empirically unfalsifiable). To avoid this uncomfortable conclusion, while also keeping sensory phenomenology at the correct timescale, we suggest that phenomenology in our model is most plausibly situated at the point during which (and based on the manner in which) lower-level representations update the content of higher-level states

span.label: the consistent parameter set - FITTED, WITH THE AUTHORS' ARGUMENT FOR WHY IT STILL COUNTS: the values were finetuned to capture behaviour reported in the literature, and the authors argue that no consistent set need have existed, so finding one supports the model
span.quote: This should not be a surprise, as we finetuned the parameter values to capture behaviour reported in the empirical literature. However, it is worth noting that it is possible a priori that no consistent set of parameter values could be found to reproduce all of these known empirical results – which would have shown a clear insufficiency of the model. Thus, the existence of this consistent set of parameter values does support the validity of the model

span.label: extends → the global neuronal workspace (GNW) model
span.quote: Here we aim to make progress in overcoming these limitations by advancing an extension of the global neuronal workspace - the predictive global neuronal workspace (PGNW) - that unifies essential aspects of the GNW with the more recent (Bayesian) Active Inference approach to understanding brain function.

span.label: builds-on → Hohwy (2013), Whyte (2019), and Friston et al (2012)
span.quote: Formalising ideas first introduced by Hohwy (2013), Whyte (2019), and Friston et al (2012), we will argue that conscious access or “ignition” is a fundamentally inferential process that depends upon a level of processing of sufficient temporal depth to contextualise and coordinate lower levels of processing.

span.label: contradicts → Fleming's (2019) higher-order state-space (HOSS) model
span.quote: Although this is ultimately an empirical question, we regard the explicit representation of the absence of a stimulus in the perceptual state space to be a somewhat unrealistic idealisation.

span.label: P3 —distinct-from→ conscious access
span.quote: This result was recently replicated in a standard masking paradigm (Cohen, et al., 2020) showing unequivocally that the P3 is related to task relevance and is not a necessary signature of conscious access

span.label: task relevance —contrasted-with→ conscious access
span.quote: This result was recently replicated in a standard masking paradigm (Cohen, et al., 2020) showing unequivocally that the P3 is related to task relevance and is not a necessary signature of conscious access

span.label: variational Bayesian inference
span.quote: we specified the task in terms of a generative model which was inverted using a variational message passing scheme (for technical details see Parr et al., 2019a

span.label: parameter fitting (grid search)
span.quote: We settled on the specific parameters shown above by searching the parameter space to find consistent values that best reproduced the behavioural results reported in the empirical literature, while remaining within plausible limits

span.label: With one consistent parameter set the simulated agent reproduced the GNW four-way taxonomy behaviourally: weak signal plus absent attention gave chance forced-choice performance and almost no 'seen' reports.
span.quote: When signal strength was low and attention absent, the agent displayed chance levels of forced-choice performance (47%) and only reported having seen the square on 10% of trials.

span.label: Simulated first-level ERPs, corresponding to early components such as P100 and N100, barely changed with visibility.
span.quote: Here we found that ERPs at the first level of the model – which correspond to early components such as the P100 and N100 – are relatively unaffected by changes in visibility.

span.label: Simulated second-level ERPs, corresponding to the late P3, were strongly modulated by visibility, matching the empirical early-versus-late ERP dissociation.
span.quote: In contrast, ERPs at the second level – which correspond to late components, and specifically the P3 – appear to be strongly modulated by changes in visibility.

span.label: The model reproduced the Pitts inattentional-blindness dissociation: only in phase three, when the square was both seen and task-relevant, did a large late P3-like ERP appear.
span.quote: Finally, in phase three, when the model was attending to the internal stimulus, the square was reported on 100% of trials and there was a large and late ERP at the second level resembling the P3.

span.label: The model yields the testable prediction that a late ERP accompanies conscious access only when high-level confidence shifts quickly, so awareness without a P3 is possible.
span.quote: it leads to a straightforward prediction; visual consciousness will be accompanied by a late ERP whenever confidence in a particular state at a high level of the hierarchy changes rapidly.

span.label: Adding prior expectation as a third factor, expectations consistent with the stimulus raised both forced-choice accuracy and the rate of 'seen' reports in every quadrant of the taxonomy.
span.quote: Across all taxonomy conditions, we found that consistent prior expectations increased both the accuracy of forced-choice behaviour and the percentage of trials where the model reported having seen the stimulus

span.label: With a strong attended stimulus, a consistent prior shrank the simulated P3 while an inconsistent prior enlarged it relative to neutral priors.
span.quote: the amplitude of ERPs at the second level of the model, corresponding to the P3, were dampened by a consistent prior and boosted by an inconsistent prior relative to neutral priors.

span.label: The model reconciles univariate ignition results with multivariate decoding of unseen stimuli, because above-baseline firing persists on unconscious trials and would be readable by a classifier even though mean rates are lower.
span.quote: although firing rates are higher for conscious compared to unconscious conditions, there is still a greater than baseline firing rate in unconscious conditions at both the firstand second-level within our simulations that could easily be exploited by a classifier.

span.label: global workspace theory (GWT)
span.quote: GWT was first proposed by Baars (1988) as a cognitive architecture that identifies consciousness with the global availability of information.

span.label: global neuronal workspace (GNW) model
span.quote: Dehaene and colleagues have advanced a global neuronal workspace (GNW) model, which identifies the global workspace with a large-scale network of excitatory pyramidal neurons with long-range axonal pathways connecting prefrontal and parietal cortices

span.label: ignition
span.quote: The key working hypothesis of the GNW is that when a stimulus becomes conscious there will be a late, non-linear, all-ornothing “ignition” of prefrontal and parietal regions

span.label: access consciousness
span.quote: this paper is chiefly concerned with what Block (2005) terms “access consciousness” which is defined as the availability of information for verbal report, voluntary action, and executive processing.

span.label: predictive global neuronal workspace (PGNW)
span.quote: Here we aim to make progress in overcoming these limitations by advancing an extension of the global neuronal workspace - the predictive global neuronal workspace (PGNW) - that unifies essential aspects of the GNW with the more recent (Bayesian) Active Inference approach to understanding brain function.

span.label: Active Inference
span.quote: Active Inference, a corollary of the free energy principle (FEP), is a first principles approach to modelling (approximately) Bayes optimal behaviour

span.label: partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP)
span.quote: POMDPs model discrete transitions between latent variables and the observations they generate.

span.label: attention (precision of the internal-stimulus likelihood mapping)
span.term: attention (precision of the internal-stimulus likelihood mapping)
span.quote: We manipulated attention by requiring the agent to monitor the colour of the surrounding circles (either red or black) at the expense of the inner array

span.label: stimulus signal strength (presentation time or contrast)
span.term: stimulus signal strength (presentation time or contrast)
span.quote: To model manipulations of attention and stimulus signal strength, we manipulated the precision of the mapping between hidden states and the outcomes encoded in the first-level A matrix by passing what were initially identity matrices through two softmax (normalized exponential) functions controlled by two precision parameters, and , respectively encoding attention and signal strength

span.label: prior expectation about the stimulus sequence (second-level D vector)
span.term: prior expectation about the stimulus sequence (second-level D vector)
span.quote: we altered the prior probability of the “square present” sequence in the second level D vector for each of the four parameter settings used in the fourway taxonomy

span.label: forced-choice accuracy and rate of 'seen' reports
span.term: forced-choice accuracy and rate of 'seen' reports
span.quote: When signal strength increased, or when the agent attended to the stimulus, forced choice performance improved to well above chance, 58% and 61% respectively

span.label: simulated neuronal firing rates
span.quote: We next simulated the neural firing rates associated with the different quadrants of the taxonomy. The simulated firstand second-level firing rates both accurately reproduced a number of otherwise disparate empirical findings

span.label: belief-decay (mdp.erp) parameter
span.quote: Here we do not include this parameter (i.e., we set it to a value of 1), which entails that posterior beliefs at one timepoint fully carry over as priors for the subsequent timepoint in a trial.

span.label: first-level state transitions (B matrices)
span.quote: The state transitions specified by the B matrices were all identity matrices, meaning that the hidden states were stable across the course of each trial.

span.label: 200 trials — size of the proof-of-principle simulation, half with the square present
span.quote: As a proof of principle, we simulated 200 trials, 100 of which were “square-present” trials.

span.label: 100% — forced-choice and report accuracy of the model under full attention and high signal strength
span.quote: We found that the model performed with 100% accuracy on the forcedchoice task and when reporting the presence – and absence – of the square (see figure 4).

span.label: 47% — chance-level forced-choice accuracy in the weak-signal, attention-absent quadrant
span.quote: When signal strength was low and attention absent, the agent displayed chance levels of forced-choice performance (47%) and only reported having seen the square on 10% of trials.

span.label: 58% and 61% — forced-choice accuracy when signal strength alone, or attention alone, was raised
span.quote: When signal strength increased, or when the agent attended to the stimulus, forced choice performance improved to well above chance, 58% and 61% respectively

span.label: 53% — rate at which the calibrated model reported seeing the square in phase one of the simulated inattentional-blindness task, matching the human 50%
span.quote: Through stimulus strength calibration, in phase one the model reported the presence of the square 53% of the time, mirroring the empirical results.

span.label: 800 — square-present trials simulated for the expectation-extended taxonomy, 100 per prior-by-quadrant cell
span.quote: We presented the model with 800 “square present” trials, 100 corresponding to “consistent prior” and “inconsistent prior” conditions, for each of the four parameter settings used in the four-way taxonomy.

p.note: The full text of this article is not redistributable, so it is not included here. Every tag above carries the exact sentence it was made from, quoted under fair quotation. The article itself is at https://doi.org/10.1016/j.pneurobio.2020.101918.
